name: MIPI
seoDesc: MIPI: work out MIPI from the age in years and the serum LDH. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the age in years, the serum LDH and the white Blood Cells and the MIPI calculator solves for MIPI. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing repaints underneath you: edit a field, press Calculate, and the new answer appears. That is how you find out which input the result is sensitive to.

sections.title: How does the MIPI calculator work?
sections.html:
The MIPI calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports MIPI in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the ECOG); then you type in the age in years, the serum LDH and the white Blood Cells.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in years. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as 0-1 and 2-4. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in U/l.
  • A number, expressed in × 1000/µl.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “I know the level of Ki-67 (optional)”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in percent. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the MIPI calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

MIPI=((707 ÷ 20000) × age in years + (3489 ÷ 5000) × ECOG + (9393 ÷ 10000) × (1000 × white Blood Cells) + (1367 ÷ 1000) × (stos))
MIPI=(ee + ((707 ÷ 20000) × age in years + (3489 ÷ 5000) × ECOG + (9393 ÷ 10000) × (1000 × white Blood Cells) + (1367 ÷ 1000) × (stos)))
C=(1367 ÷ 1000) × (stos)
Upper normal limit of serum LDH=serum LDH ÷ stos
D=(9393 ÷ 10000) × (1000 × white Blood Cells)
Ee=(1071 ÷ 50000) × ki-67

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose ECOG set to 0-1 and Upper normal limit of serum LDH = 160. Working through the relationship above gives Serum LDH = 1600.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Serum LDH = 1600 should be roughly the size you expected from ECOG set to 0-1 and Upper normal limit of serum LDH = 160.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Time, opening in years
  • %, opening in percent

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The MIPI calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the age in years, the serum LDH and the white Blood Cells — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the MIPI calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns MIPI, derived from the age in years, the serum LDH and the white Blood Cells. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the MIPI calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the age in years, the serum LDH and the white Blood Cells, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter age in years in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Age in years opens in years and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Serum LDH = 1600. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the MIPI calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
